title: Ensuring Safety and Trust: Analyzing the Risks of Large Language Models in Medicine

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual substitution of a patient's biological gender (male, female) in clinical case prompts (e.g., mortality risk and cost prediction) to evaluate if the model's predictions remain consistent.
Counterfactual substitution of a patient's race or ethnicity (Asian, Black, Hispanic, White) in clinical case prompts to evaluate if the model's predictions remain consistent.

Multiple-choice questions requiring the model to distinguish between respectful statements and inappropriate, stigmatizing, or stereotypical statements regarding patients with specific diseases and conditions (e.g., HIV, mental disorders, obesity, physical disability).
Comparing model accuracy on medical multiple-choice questions translated into Spanish and Chinese to evaluate performance disparities and robustness across different languages.
